assumptions: Systemic failure in intelligent agents can be operationalized as utility function drift or objective divergence.
Cognitive architecture constraints regarding planning and execution are distinct and separable.
Feedback latency acts as a measurable bottleneck for self-correction mechanisms.
definition.falsification: Observed failure rates remain stable or decrease as feedback latency increases, or if failure rates are independent of planning-execution cycle duration.
definition.statement: Increased feedback latency in intelligent systems, during the transition from plan formulation to solution execution, results in a non-linear increase in utility function drift and systemic failure, specifically when the system's operational environment changes faster than its metareasoning cycle.
definition.uncertainty: The magnitude of 'utility function drift' relative to specific latency thresholds remains theoretically underspecified without experimental baseline data.

proposal.summary: This proposal establishes an experimental hypothesis on the relationship between feedback latency and utility function stability in intelligent systems, utilizing evidence on cognitive architecture constraints and planning-execution gaps.
proposal.title: Formalizing Feedback Latency and Systemic Failure Hypothesis
